newsitem.title: UK: Traders expect more delays to IPE gas contract.
newsitem.headline: Traders expect more delays to IPE gas contract.

text.p: The long-delayed launch of a natural gas forward contract on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) looks to have run into fresh problems and is unlikely to take place before the end of the year, gas industry sources said on Friday.

Last month, IPE director of business development Richard Ward said he hoped the National Balancing Point (NBP) contract would launched this year but did not specify a date, which was initially set for November.
"We still can't set a date," an IPE spokesman said on Friday.
The IPE's initial plan to launch a contract at the Bacton beach terminal was stalled by problems of physical delivery verification.
In early summer the Exchange decided to change tack and focused its efforts on a contract based at the NBP, a notional trading point within the Transco pipeline network.
But the launch of this contract has run into its own problems, traders said.
"The IPE has been slow in realising how many agreements they need to get the NBP contract in place, such as Network Code adjustments," said a would-be natural gas futures broker.
"It was not thought out properly when they decided in June to launch the contract and said it would be ready by autumn."

The contract requires modification to the Network Code -- the rulebook for gas shippers -- in order for the IPE clearing house to gain access to the A.T. link screen system which shows trade nominations at the NBP.
The industry regulator Ofgas has to approve the modification and then get the go-ahead from shippers.
While the IPE says it has been assured by Ofgas that "things can move ahead quickly", potential users of the NBP contract are not expecting the launch for several months.
"We have put a lot of marketing effort into promoting this contract and the length of time it's taking is very frustrating." said the broker.
Another sticking point could be the IPE's plans for the contract to trade just three months ahead.
"The industry wants something to trade at least one year forward. The OTC (over-the-counter) market is already trading even further ahead than that," said a trader for a major gas shipper.
A possible reason for the IPE's reluctance to launch a longer-term contract is an idea mooted by British Gas's pipeline arm Transco to split the NBP into three regional trading points.
"The IPE is loath to base a contract on something that might change, therefore they only want to launch a contract for something two or three months forward," said the natural gas broker.

Arguments over the NBP contract have diverted attention from the original Bacton proposal which is still dogged by the failure of the Claims Validation Agent (CVA) to come up with an effective mechanism for the verification of physical deliveries of gas at the beach.
The same issues are also undermining Bacton's popularity among gas buyers as the basis for over-the-counter trades, say traders.
The NBP, which first came into use in the spring, now claims around two thirds of spot trade, and has stolen Bacton's role as the benchmark trading hub.
"The NBP has no tolerances, no shortfalls, no force majeure...If you are buying you know you are going to get the gas you asked for," said a trader for a leading U.K. shipper.
"I'd say 90 percent of the trades we do now are at the NBP," he added.
The need for daily balancing in the pipeline system since the Network Code "hard landing" on Oct.1 has also encouraged small volume trade at the NBP, traders said.
"It's a lot easier to balance at NBP but big trades of 100,000 therms upwards are still carried out at the beach terminals," said one North Sea producer with trading interests at Bacton.
But the opening of the Interconnector gas pipeline, from Bacton to Zeebrugge in Belgium, slated for 1998, should eventually restore Bacton as the predominant trading hub.
Access to the European gas market is behind the IPE's refusal to shelve plans for a Bacton forward contract despite its drawbacks.

"Delivery at Bacton is open to a larger number of participants, both producers and shippers, and this will increase further when the Interconnector comes onstream. Our aspirations are European, not just domestic," said the IPE official.
-Rosalind Russell, London Newsroom +44 171 542 5387
